channel.title: US Visa Policy (English)
channel.description: USCIS and State Department policy updates in five languages

item.title: DHS Publicizes Five ICE Arrests of Immigrants in Michigan With Criminal Records
item.description: DHS issued a press release describing five noncitizens arrested by ICE in Grand Rapids and Detroit, Michigan between October 12 and 18, 2026, listing their alleged criminal histories and immigration status. The release announces no new policy, fee, or eligibility change.

item.title: USCIS Allows Fee-Free Reopening for Sileiri Doe Class Members Hit by 2025 CBP One Parole Terminations
item.description: Following a September 28, 2026 federal court order in Sileiri Doe v. DHS, USCIS will accept fee-free requests to reopen or reconsider certain adverse immigration decisions from people whose CBP One parole was terminated in April 2025. The process applies to USCIS decisions issued between April 1, 2025 and April 21, 2026, excludes employment-authorization requests based on parole, and has no filing deadline.

item.title: DHS Ratifies Civil Penalties Issued Under Interim Immigration Rule, Sets Nov. 16 Deadline
item.description: DHS has ratified all final civil penalty decisions issued between June 27, 2025, and October 13, 2026, under an interim rule covering certain immigration violations. The interim rule became a final rule on October 14, 2026, with only one substantive change allowing late appeals in cases of proven mail delays. Individuals who believe they were prejudiced by the interim procedures can submit a claim to ICE by November 16, 2026.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Arrests of Five Noncitizens With Criminal Histories in Georgia
item.description: DHS released a statement describing five noncitizens arrested by ICE in Georgia between October 13 and 18, 2026, citing their criminal histories. The statement, issued by DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, also referenced the Laken Riley Act.

item.title: HSI and FBI Arrest Ten Non-Citizens for Alleged Voter Fraud in North Carolina
item.description: DHS announced that HSI, ICE's investigative arm, and the FBI arrested ten non-citizens in North Carolina on October 14 and 15, 2026, including nine lawful permanent residents and one person DHS describes as in the country illegally. All ten were charged with voting by an alien and false claims to U.S. citizenship, with illegal voting dating back as far as 1998.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Noncitizens Convicted of Murder and Sex Crimes
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced the arrests of five noncitizens with prior criminal convictions, including first-degree murder, sexual abuse of a minor, enticement of a minor, and incest, in a press release describing ongoing enforcement operations. The individuals, from Vietnam, Mexico, Jamaica and Guatemala, were convicted in separate cases in Florida, Maryland, Utah, Connecticut and Missouri.

item.title: DHS Statement: Illegal Alien, Former DACA Recipient, Charged in Iwo Jima Memorial Attack
item.description: DHS said a man was arrested for using a sledgehammer to decapitate a statue at the Iwo Jima Memorial in Quantico, Virginia, on the evening of October 21. The suspect, identified as Miguel Alonso Maldonado Soriano, entered the U.S. illegally in 1999 and was granted DACA in 2014, which has since expired.

item.title: State Department Renames Passport Records System, Updates Privacy Act Notice
item.description: The Department of State has published a modified System of Records Notice renaming its Passport Records system to Passport Services Records (State-26). The changes reflect a move to cloud storage, new OMB guidance, and expanded uses of passport data for identity verification by other agencies.

item.title: DHS Publicizes ICE Arrests of Immigrants with Criminal Records in Iowa
item.description: DHS issued a press release naming five individuals arrested by ICE in Iowa between October 1 and October 16, 2026, each described as having entered the United States illegally and having prior criminal convictions. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the arrests reflect the agency's continued effort to find and remove undocumented immigrants with criminal histories nationwide.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Criminal Aliens Convicted of Trafficking and Robbery
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested five individuals described as criminal illegal aliens, each previously convicted of offenses including conspiracy to transport illegal aliens, drug trafficking, and robbery. The announcement is part of ICE's ongoing enforcement activity targeting noncitizens with criminal convictions.

item.title: Six Charged in Massachusetts Marriage Fraud Ring, USCIS Assisted Investigation
item.description: The U.S. Attorney for the District of Massachusetts announced charges against six individuals accused of running a sham marriage scheme that helped illegal aliens obtain immigration status over more than a decade. USCIS, ICE, and other federal agencies assisted in the investigation.

item.title: Sacramento Grocery Manager Convicted of Immigration Document Fraud, Obstructing Labor Probes
item.description: Karla Montoya, general manager of Viva Supermarkets in the Sacramento area, was found guilty at trial of immigration document fraud, conspiracy, and obstructing two Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division investigations. USCIS says it assisted the case, which was announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of California.

item.title: Two Canadian Nationals in Idaho Charged With Illegal Voting
item.description: USCIS assisted an investigation by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Idaho that led to charges against two Canadian nationals accused of voting in the 2022 general election despite not being U.S. citizens. Both defendants face felony charges carrying significant fines and potential prison time if convicted. The release notes the charges are allegations and the defendants are presumed innocent.

item.title: State Department Bars 15 Named Bolivian Officials Over Corruption, Narcotrafficking Ties
item.description: The Department of State announced visa restrictions on 40 individuals in Bolivia under a policy first announced on September 28, 2026, and this release names 15 of them. The restrictions, imposed under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, target people accused of using corruption or narcotrafficking to undermine Bolivia's democratically elected government.

item.title: State Department Imposes Visa Restrictions on 21 Colombians Over Corruption, Narcotrafficking
item.description: The Department of State announced visa restrictions on 21 individuals in Colombia under a policy first announced on September 28, 2026, citing corruption and narcotrafficking that undermine democratically elected governments in the hemisphere. The announcement names seven of the individuals, including a former Ecopetrol president, a sitting mayor, and several current and former legislators.

item.title: DHS Statement After Attempted Firebombing of ICE Facility in Atlanta
item.description: On the evening of October 20, 2026, a man threw an improvised incendiary device toward the ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) field office in Atlanta, but the device became caught on the facility's perimeter fence and did not reach the building. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called the incident part of an escalating pattern of violence against ICE personnel.

item.title: South African Lawful Permanent Resident Charged With Unlawful Voting in 2024 Election
item.description: USCIS said a South African national and lawful permanent resident living in Missouri has been charged with unlawfully voting in the November 2024 federal election. The case was investigated by ICE's Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS, and is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Convicted Criminal Immigrants in Multiple States
item.description: ICE said it arrested five immigrants without legal status who have prior criminal convictions, including rape, assault with a firearm, and drug trafficking, in separate incidents in New York, California, Utah, Oklahoma, and Texas. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the arrests are part of ongoing enforcement operations targeting criminal aliens.

item.title: DHS Publicizes ICE Arrests of Five Undocumented Immigrants in South Carolina
item.description: DHS issued a press release on October 21, 2026, describing ICE arrests of five individuals in South Carolina between July and October 2026, citing criminal histories including arson, aggravated assault and gang activity. The release includes a statement from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin about ICE enforcement priorities.

item.title: DHS Announces ICE Arrests Over Alleged SNAP Benefit Fraud, Signals Larger Crackdown
item.description: DHS announced that ICE has arrested several illegal aliens accused of fraudulently receiving SNAP benefits intended for U.S. citizens. DHS described these arrests as the first phase of a sustained, large-scale enforcement operation targeting SNAP fraud by illegal aliens.

item.title: CBP Extends Compliance Deadline for Mail Shipment De Minimis Rule to January 2027
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has extended, from October 22, 2026 to January 20, 2027, the compliance date for formal entry requirements on certain postal shipments affected by the suspension of the de minimis exemption. The rule is a customs and trade measure and does not concern visas, immigration status or citizenship.

item.title: CBP Modifies Test of Electronic Informal Mail Entry Process
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection is modifying its test of the new electronic informal entry process (entry type 13) for low-value international mail shipments. This notice concerns customs entry procedures and is not related to U.S. visas or immigration.

item.title: Canadian National Indicted for Illegal Voting in Federal Election in Kentucky
item.description: A federal grand jury in Louisville, Kentucky indicted Sandra Madeline Watson, a Canadian alien, for illegally voting in a federal election. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Kentucky announced the charge, with USCIS assisting the investigation.

item.title: DHS Highlights Five ICE Arrests of Noncitizens with Criminal Records in North Carolina
item.description: DHS issued a press release describing five noncitizens arrested by ICE in North Carolina in recent weeks, each with prior criminal convictions. The release includes a statement from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin defending the administration's immigration enforcement priorities. The announcement reports on individual enforcement actions already taken and does not change any immigration law, rule, or policy.

item.title: Florida Woman Sentenced to 15 Months for Assaulting ICE and CBP Officers
item.description: DHS announced that a U.S. citizen was sentenced to 15 months in prison for assaulting an ICE officer, a CBP officer, and a Florida Highway Patrol trooper during a January immigration enforcement stop in Jacksonville, Florida. She was also sentenced to two years of supervised release and ordered to pay restitution.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Noncitizens With Criminal Convictions, Including Child Sex Abuse Case
item.description: ICE announced the arrest of five unauthorized immigrants convicted of serious crimes, including continuous sexual abuse of a child under 16, aggravated assault, and endangering the welfare of a child. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin issued a statement defending the agency's enforcement operations.

item.title: Massachusetts Man Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud and Fraudulent Use of Federal Seals
item.description: Mario Cesar Dos Santos, Jr. pleaded guilty to wire fraud and fraudulent use of government seals after running a fake agency called CEMA that falsely claimed FEMA endorsement and sold bogus chaplaincy credentials. USCIS assisted in the investigation, which was led by the DHS Office of Inspector General and the FBI. He falsely told attendees their CEMA status would protect them from immigration enforcement and deportation.

item.title: DHS Secretary and CBP Commissioner Tour Arizona Cargo Facility, Oversee Deportation Flights
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott visited a CBP cargo inspection facility at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport to review how CBP screens imported goods for contraband and mislabeled products. The same day, Mullin oversaw deportation flights from Arizona removing individuals to Mexico.

item.title: DHS: ICE Arrests Illegal Aliens Convicted of Murder, Child Sex Abuse, Rape and Drug Trafficking
item.description: DHS announced that over a recent weekend, ICE arrested a number of unlawfully present individuals with criminal convictions including felony murder, lewd acts with a child under 14, rape, strangulation, burglary and drug trafficking. The release lists individual cases by name, country of origin, conviction and location across several states.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Arrests of Illegal Immigrants with Criminal Records in Kansas
item.description: DHS released a statement and photos highlighting five people described as illegal aliens with criminal histories arrested by ICE in Kansas in recent months. The cited convictions include murder, sexual offenses against a child, rape, drug trafficking and robbery.

item.title: Massachusetts Man Indicted in Sham Marriage Scheme to Obtain Green Card
item.description: A federal grand jury indicted a Massachusetts man for conspiracy to commit marriage fraud and immigration document fraud after USCIS and ICE Homeland Security Investigations assisted in the probe. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced the charges.

item.title: Rhode Island Immigration Attorney Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud, Tax Evasion
item.description: A former immigration attorney in Providence, Rhode Island pleaded guilty to wire fraud and tax evasion for defrauding immigration clients of about $98,000 between 2019 and 2023. USCIS assisted the investigation, which was led by ICE Homeland Security Investigations, the IRS, the Providence Police Department and the FBI.

item.title: ICE Reports Arrests of More Than 100 Gang Members in Under a Week
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested 131 gang-affiliated individuals between October 4 and October 10, 2026, including members of MS-13 and Tren de Aragua. DHS said that since January 20, 2025, ICE has made 12,018 gang-related administrative arrests nationwide.

item.title: DHS orders exclusion and removal of DeepSeek products from federal civilian IT systems
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has issued an order, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, excluding IT products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd from federal civilian agency procurement and requiring removal of existing DeepSeek-related products from federal civilian IT systems. This notice concerns federal procurement and cybersecurity, not immigration, visas, or citizenship.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Immigrants Convicted of Murder, Child Sex Crimes and Drug Trafficking
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said it arrested several individuals in the country illegally who have prior convictions for serious crimes, including murder, child pornography, cocaine trafficking and fraud conspiracy. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said ICE will continue enforcing immigration law against those who commit crimes.

item.title: DHS, Transportation and War Departments Impose Drone Flight Restriction Over Southern Border
item.description: DHS, the Department of Transportation and the Department of War announced a temporary flight restriction (TFR) barring unauthorized drone activity along the U.S.-Mexico border. The measure is an airspace security and aviation safety action, not a change to visa or immigration procedures.

item.title: DHS Secretary and CBP Commissioner Tour Border Wall in Arizona
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott visited the southern border in Arizona to view ongoing border wall construction. The visit coincided with the administration marking 17 months of what it called zero releases of illegal aliens and the lowest fiscal year border crossing numbers on record.

item.title: DHS Secretary Oversees Deportation Flights of Convicted Noncitizens From Arizona
item.description: On October 16, 2026, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin oversaw deportation flights departing Phoenix, Arizona, removing noncitizens to Mexico. DHS described the individuals as having criminal convictions or arrests for offenses including child sexual abuse, assault, drug trafficking, DUI, and gang activity, with several having prior deportations and illegal reentries.

item.title: DHS Reports Record Low Fiscal Year 2026 Southwest Border Crossings
item.description: DHS and CBP announced preliminary Fiscal Year 2026 data showing a 95 percent drop in southwest border apprehensions compared to the Biden administration and the lowest annual encounters in U.S. history. The agencies also reported the first fiscal year on record with zero Border Patrol releases.

item.title: ICE Investigation Leads to Conviction of Mexican National in Minnesota Child Pornography Case
item.description: A federal jury convicted Alejandro Rojas Garcia, a Mexican national without legal immigration status, of attempted production of child pornography following an investigation by ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) in Minnesota. He faces a mandatory minimum 15-year sentence and, according to DHS, will be deported after completing his sentence.
